title: Pharmacy Sales & Profitability Dashboard
summary: Power BI analysis of $8.63M in pharmacy sales, finding what drives performance across products, regions, store sizes and cities.
problem: Pharmacy performance was uneven across products, regions, store formats and cities, with no single view of where revenue and profit actually came from.
objective: Show revenue and profit trends, category performance and differences by store size and location, and point to where growth should be prioritised.
approach: Built a two-page Power BI report (Overview, and Sales & Profitability) with headline KPI cards, Year, Quarter, Month and Day drill-down, and breakdowns by category, store size and location (country, region and city).
process: Explored the dataset and defined the business questions: which products, regions and store types drive performance
Built KPI cards for cost, revenue, units sold, profit margin and transaction count
Added revenue and profit trends with Year, Quarter, Month and Day drill-down to show seasonality
Broke sales down by product category, store size and top cities, with Country, Region and City views
Summarised the findings and growth opportunities in a LinkedIn write-up

results.text: $8.63M revenue and $2.42M profit, a 28% profit margin, from 446K units across 62K transactions
OTC led all categories with 19.4K sales, ahead of Prescription (13.1K) and Wellness (12.5K)
Urban pharmacies generated $4.1M in revenue, against $3.1M for Suburban and $1.4M for Rural
Medium stores led with 28.2K sales, ahead of Large (19.8K) and Small (14.2K)
Monthly revenue ranged from $0.5M to $1.0M, with peaks mid-year and towards year-end
Milan (3.5K) and Hamburg (3.1K) led city sales, while the lowest cities recorded about 2.1K

impact: Shows that growth is concentrated in high-density markets, OTC products and medium-format stores, giving leadership a clear basis to decide whether to prioritise products, regions or store strategy.
